pr_body:
This commit allows Action Text to be used without having an `ApplicationController` defined.  In doing so, it also fixes Action Text attachments to render the correct URL host in mailers.

It also avoids allocating an `ActionController::Renderer` per request.

Fixes #37183.
Fixes #35578.
Fixes #36963.
Closes #38714.

---

TODO:
* [x] more tests

/cc @jeremy  I started tinkering on #37183, and found it overlapped with the issues listed above.  Notably #36963, which you were working on.  What do you think about this approach?  It differs a bit from #38714 in that it uses the current controller instance, and so can work with a mailer (to fix #35578).  Since I took inspiration from #38714, I've added you as a co-author.

issue_context.title: Misleading deprecation warning when referencing ActionController::Base
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce
- Create a new app with Rails 6.0.0.rc1.
- Add a reference to `ActionController::Base` to `config/application.rb`.
- Run `bundle install`.
- Run `rails environment`.
- Run `cat log/development.log`.

### Expected behavior
The `development.log` file should be empty.

### Actual behavior
The log file contains the following deprecation warning:

```
DEPRECATION WARNING: Initialization autoloaded the constants ActionText::ContentHelper and ActionText::TagHelper.

Being able to do this is deprecated. Autoloading during initialization is going
to be an error condition in future versions of Rails.

Reloading does not reboot the application, and therefore code executed during
initialization does not run again. So, if you reload ActionText::ContentHelper, for example,
the expected changes won't be reflected in that stale Module object.

These autoloaded constants have been unloaded.

Please, check the "Autoloading and Reloading Constants" guide for solutions.
 (called from <main> at /Users/
USER/Projects/rails-app-test/config/environment.rb:5)
```

A few thoughts:
- Referencing `ActionController::Base` from an initializer may be poor form, but that is neither documented nor indicated by the warning.
- I cannot tell whether ActionText's helper modules are *intentionally* passing through the autoloader.  Most Rails code *doesn't seem to*, but maybe Engine code is exceptional?
- Tracking down what was causing these autoloads was tricky, involving monkeypatches to `ActiveSupport::Dependencies` and direct edits to the Rails source files loaded by Bundler.

(I have filed a related bug with another project, including a detailed outline of the observed causal chain.  rollbar/rollbar-gem/issues/880)

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.0.0.rc1
**Ruby version**: 2.6.3
comments: Can confirm this is still an issue in `6.0.0.rc2`.

Still happening in 6.0.0. In my app I had references to `ActiveSupport::Logger` and `ActiveSupport::TaggedLogging` in my config/application.rb which was causing the zeitwerk deprecation notices about `ActionText::ContentHelper` and `ActionText::TagHelper`. This was also causing zeitwerk deprecation notices about all my sidekiq workers for that machine. Inserting `require "active_support/logger"` and `require "active_support/tagged_logging"` didn't remove those warnings.

I wrapped the Logger and TaggedLogging references in a `ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller) do` block and that got rid of the issue on startup. Still working on getting rid of those warnings for rspec though.

**Update:** Also happening in 6.0.1. The `ActiveSupport.on_load` block appears to break STDOUT. Still looking for a proper solution.

> Tracking down what was causing these autoloads was tricky, involving monkeypatches to ActiveSupport::Dependencies and direct edits to the Rails source files loaded by Bundler.

@pvande have you, or could you, document the process you followed to identify the root cause? I'm looking to do the same in my app and am not sure where to start. Thanks!
+1 for describe the root cause(s) in the warning. Just point to config/environment.rb gives no idea where to look

Got this in my app on 6.0.1, the warning was caused by several old gems trying to `include` their helpers into `ActionController::Base` in engine initializer/railtie, which caused loading of helpers.
Gems were `wicked_pdf`(opened a PR with a fix there), `split`(new version is already fixed) and old version of `twitter-bootstrap-rails`.

To track this I used an initializer with:
```ruby
ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller_base) do
  bc = ActiveSupport::BacktraceCleaner.new
  bc.remove_silencers!
  bc.add_silencer { |line| line.start_with?(RbConfig::CONFIG["rubylibdir"]) }
  bc.add_silencer { |line| line =~ Regexp.union(
    *(
      %w{ bootsnap railties spring activesupport actionpack zeitwerk thor rack }.
      map{|g| /\A#{g} \([\w.]+\) /}
    ),
    /\Abin\/rails/
  )}
  trace = bc.clean(caller)
  puts "Cleaned backtrace:\n\t#{trace.join("\n\t")}\n"
  puts "Most probably the cause is: #{trace.first}"
  puts "If not - uncomment `raise` at #{__FILE__}:#{__LINE__+1}"
  # raise "i can haz full backtrace"
  exit(1)
end
```
and spotted gems and my own initializers in the backtrace, like:
> Most probably the cause is: split (3.3.2) lib/split/engine.rb:6:in \`block in <class:Engine>'
> If not - uncomment `raise` at \<initializer filename here\>

Hello! @Vasfed thanks a lot for the initilializer. Would you have a link to the proposed fixes in `wicked_pdf`, `split` and `twitter-bootstrap-rails` to get an idea of the PR to propose for `remotipart`?
@vdegove Looks like `remotipart` (used by `rails_admin`) already has an open PR https://github.com/JangoSteve/remotipart/pull/206

I am seeing it just after adding rails-admin v 2.0.0, so it is it or some of its dependency.

And found it is already filed: https://github.com/sferik/rails_admin/issues/3190 

For anyone who lands here.
Wicked_pdf has an open PR here: https://github.com/mileszs/wicked_pdf/pull/869

Getting incredibly confused by this while working on the Sorcery rework. When using @Vasfed's example above, it points at the `ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller_base) do` call itself as what's causing Zeitwerk deprecation warnings. Not sure how that's possible, nor how to address it... If anyone has an idea please let me know. If I figure it out, I'll follow up here for anyone else similarly confused in the future.

Issue appeared to be calling `require 'rspec/rails'` in the wrong order.

This causes deprecation warnings:
```ruby
require 'rails/all'
require 'rspec/rails'
require 'dummy_app/config/environment'
```
To fix, move the require below your application call:

```ruby
require 'rails/all'
require 'dummy_app/config/environment'
require 'rspec/rails'
```

We had these deprecation warnings but only if `RAILS_ENV=test`. I didn't manage to figure out why but changing from `require "rails/all"` in `application.rb` to requiring individual parts of rails and skipping to require `rails/action_text` got rid of the warnings. Simple fix for anyone who doesn't actually make use of ActionText.

From what I've seen there is always some code using ActionController "too early" whenever this warning is emitted. On the rails app I saw this on:

* there was a gem being loaded that was patching/referencing ActionController without using `ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller)`, causing ActionController to be loaded early
* when the ActionText initializer runs ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller), ActionController is already loaded so the block to load helpers runs immediately, autoloading ActionText::ContentHelper

How I diagnosed it - I put a debugger in the action_controller/base.rb to figure out the first thing to load it. Going up in the stack trace, it lead me to the code referencing ActionController without ActiveSupport.on_load

How I fixed it - I updated the code in the gem to use ActiveSupport.on_load:

```
-module ActionController
-  module MyGemStuff
-    def self.included(klass)
-      klass.extend(ClassMethods)
-    end
+ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller) do
+  module ActionController
+    module MyGemStuff
+      def self.included(klass)
+        klass.extend(ClassMethods)
+      end
```

Hope this helps someone - it's like there's a gem or initializer being loaded that is the cause

EDIT: Noticed that this is just a repeat of prior comment https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/36546#issuecomment-558773961 which gives a faster way to find the culprits :)

It seems that most people are experiencing this deprecation because of a 3rd party gem, but figuring out which one is quite difficult.

In my case, it turned out that version 2.11.1 of https://github.com/kpumuk/meta-tags was the culprit. Apparently this was fixed in 2.14.0, released on December 10, 2020.
For me, there were two gems causing this issue `parallel_tests` and `rails_semantic_logger`.  Hope that helps others track down these deprecations.  There aren't any fixed versions of these gems yet.

Here's what we come up in config/application.rb 

```ruby
require "rails"

%w(
  active_record/railtie
  active_storage/engine
  action_controller/railtie
  action_view/railtie
  action_mailer/railtie
```

ref: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/initialization.html#railties-lib-rails-all-rb

after few hours I've discovered that mailgun-ruby is causing this and particularly these things:

ActionMailer::Base.add_delivery_method :mailgun, Railgun::Mailer
ActionMailer::Base.register_interceptor(OverrideAttachmentsContentId)

I've substituted `ActionMailer::Base.register_interceptor(OverrideAttachmentsContentId)` -> `Mail.register_interceptor(OverrideAttachmentsContentId)`
but nothing to do with mailgun .. dunno if it's a ActionMailer::Base bug but I guess so as I couldn't find a replacement

For me it was this in an initializer:

`ActionMailer::Base.add_delivery_method :sendgrid, SendgridDelivery`

Changing it to 

```
ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_mailer) do
  add_delivery_method :sendgrid, SendgridDelivery
end
```

Fixed it.

Thanks for the advice, all. In our case, it's in `rubycas-client`, required by `devise_cas_authenticatable`: https://github.com/nbudin/devise_cas_authenticatable/issues/151.

It happens when calling `rake test` but not `rails test`, which I think has something to do with the Spring preloader.

This chunk of code needs to be inserted in `config/application.rb` _before_ the call to `Bundler.require` so that it runs before gems run.  Obvious in hindsight, but hopefully I save someone else a few minutes of confusion.

@athix That may have been your problem with it (though I'm sure you're well past this issue by now :smile:)

In case other folks are still running into this, a bit of sleuthing revealed two sources of this deprecation warning in my Rails 6.1 app.

1) I referenced ActionMailer::Base in a couple of initializers. Based on the suggestion in the Rails Guides (https://guides.rubyonrails.org/action_mailer_basics.html#action-mailer-configuration), I decided to move all those references to environment.rb.

2) The same deprecation error was also apparently being generated by the mailgun-ruby gem v 1.2.3. It appears the deprecation warning has been fixed in v 1.2.4.
@petitJAM Thanks very much for your addition. That helped me find the culprit which was the `health_check` gem.

> This chunk of code needs to be inserted in `config/application.rb` _before_ the call to `Bundler.require` so that it runs before gems run. Obvious in hindsight, but hopefully I save someone else a few minutes of confusion.

This was amazingly helpful, thank you!

The other thing that allowed us to move beyond this was experimenting with the different hooks. The examples I've seen show to use:

`ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_controller_base)  do ...`

where we didn't see the issue until we did this:

`ActiveSupport.on_load(:action_mailer) do ...`

Our issue was with the `premailer/actionmailer_inline_css` gem. Removed this and now we're up and running.

If you are seeing this message because of using ActionMailer::Base in an initializer:

From @csutter "Instead of adding configuration to ActionMailer::Base, set it on Rails.configuration.action_mailer instead."
Making a note for myself to check if this isn't already updated in the documentation 👀

review_comments: Theoretically, this PR could also fix #38880 if `ActionController::API` also supported `helper`.

We can’t use `ActionController::Base.renderer` directly because only children of `ActionController::Base` set up their renderers, right? It’d be convenient for plugins if `ActionController::Base` had a working renderer. I don’t know if there’s a reason it can’t off the top of my head.

Can we safely assume `ActionController::Base` has been loaded here or do we need to wrap this in another load hook?

> We can’t use `ActionController::Base.renderer` directly because only children of `ActionController::Base` set up their renderers, right? It’d be convenient for plugins if `ActionController::Base` had a working renderer. I don’t know if there’s a reason it can’t off the top of my head.

Correct!  I can work on `ActionController::Base.renderer` returning a usable renderer if you'd like.  One catch would be that *if* the controller class is anonymous, we should ensure all framework code can handle an anonymous controller class.  For example, [this line](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/f04819972b75dde87276ece7c1ae9c2e57be12f2/actionview/lib/action_view/renderer/abstract_renderer.rb#L95) should be changed to `prefix&.include?(?/)`.  (That line is bypassed in this PR because of [`prefix_partial_path_with_controller_namespace = false`](https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/40222/files#diff-4737c19868c276c33d997d078ca06162R13).)  Although it might be sufficient to override `Class#name` and return a dummy value instead.

> Can we safely assume `ActionController::Base` has been loaded here or do we need to wrap this in another load hook?

I assumed it was safe because it replaces `ApplicationController`.  But also, wrapping in another load hook causes unfortunate complications.  If `ActionController::Base` has not yet been loaded, such as in a test or a mailer, then `ActionText::Content.renderer` will not be set and `ActionText::Content#to_s` will raise an error.
